Answer all questions.  For each question there are four possible answers A, B, C and D. Choose the one you consider correct and record your choice in soft pencil on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Follow the instructions on the multiple choice answer sheet.  Write in soft pencil.  Write your name, centre number and candidate number on the multiple choice answer sheet in the spaces provided unless this has been done for you.  Do not use correction fluid.  Do not write on any bar codes.  You may use a calculator. INFORMATION  The total mark for this paper is 30.  Each correct answer will score one mark.  Any rough working should be done on this question paper.
Consumers in country X buy some goods and services from private sector firms. Other goods and services are provided by the state. What is this type of economy?

options.A: free market economy
options.B: joint economy
options.C: mixed economy
options.D: planned economy

questions.questionText: In 2017 the Bank of England introduced a new version of the £1 coin as there were concerns that large quantities of illegal £1 coins had been put into circulation. Which characteristic of money did the illegal £1 coins threaten?

options.A: acceptability
options.B: divisibility
options.C: durability
options.D: portability

questions.questionText: Which statement is a positive statement?

options.A: Low inflation is preferable to low unemployment as a government aim.
options.B: Low inflation will provide a more stable macro economy.
options.C: The government must intervene in all markets to improve resource allocation.
options.D: The government should cut income tax so living standards can improve.

options.A: no no
options.B: no yes
options.C: yes no
options.D: yes yes

The diagram shows the average world price of coffee in US cents per pound weight (lb) between 1997 and 2005. US cents/lb 125 1997 2001 2005 year Which event is consistent with the price behaviour shown in the specified time period?

options.A: a continuous rise in the price of tea between 1997 and 2001
options.B: the entry to the market of new producers of coffee between 1997 and 2001
options.C: a series of good coffee harvests between 2001 and 2005
options.D: increasing health worries about drinking coffee between 2001 and 2005

What would be the price elasticity of demand for smartphones if their price fell from US$100 to US$90 and the quantity demanded rose from 200 to 250?
The diagram shows the demand for and supply of a normal good. E is the initial equilibrium position. price S E E D O quantity Which changes could result in a new equilibrium E ?

options.A: a decrease in both the demand for and the supply of the good
options.B: an increase in both the demand for and the supply of the good
options.C: an increase in consumer incomes, and a decrease in the supply of the good
options.D: an increase in the price of a complement to the good, and an increase in the supply of the good

questions.questionText: The table shows the market demand and market supply for kiwifruit over a year. At a market price of $3 per kg there is disequilibrium in the market. price of total market total market kiwifruit demand supply ($ per kg) (thousand tonnes) (thousand tonnes)

The cross-elasticity of demand of good S with respect to the price of good P is +1.5. The cross-elasticity of demand of good S with respect to the price of good R is –1.5. The cross-elasticity of demand of good P with respect to the price of good R is –1.5. What can be concluded about goods P, R and S?

options.A: S and P are complements; P and R are substitutes.
options.B: S and P are complements; R is an inferior good.
options.C: S and P are substitutes; P and R are complements.
options.D: S and P are substitutes; R is an inferior good.

questions.questionText: A government wishes to impose a tax on a good so that the consumer pays most of the tax increase. Which type of elasticity would best achieve this aim?

options.A: high price elasticity of supply
options.B: low price elasticity of supply
options.C: unitary price elasticity of supply
options.D: perfectly inelastic price elasticity of supply

questions.questionText: Why does the production of public goods have to be financed by the government?

options.A: One person’s consumption of a public good means it is not available for anyone else.
options.B: People are able to consume public goods without paying for them.
options.C: Private sector firms will charge a price significantly above cost for public goods.
options.D: The cost of producing public goods is higher in the private sector.

questions.questionText: Which payment is a transfer payment?

options.A: households’ payments of indirect taxes
options.B: government pension payments
options.C: payments between firms for the supply of raw materials
options.D: payment of salaries

A government wishes to reduce the consumption of alcohol. Which policy will it use to achieve this aim by fixing the price of alcohol?

options.A: fix maximum price above market price
options.B: fix maximum price below market price
options.C: fix minimum price above market price
options.D: fix minimum price below market price

questions.questionText: According to the theory of comparative advantage, what makes trade beneficial between two countries?

options.A: Each country has different goods to sell and different tastes.
options.B: Each country has different opportunity costs of production.
options.C: One country has the absolute advantage in producing both goods.
options.D: The prices of goods are different between each country.

questions.questionText: The demand for a country’s exports is price-elastic. Its government introduces export subsidies. What will be the effect on its balance of trade and on its terms of trade? balance of trade terms of trade

options.A: increase increase
options.B: increase decrease
options.C: decrease increase
options.D: decrease decrease

questions.questionText: The table shows the average changes in the prices and volumes of exports and imports. Which combination of changes would result in an increase in the terms of trade? export export import import prices volumes prices volumes
A government decides to increase a quota on an imported good. What is likely to happen?

options.A: The demand for the good will fall.
options.B: The good will become more expensive.
options.C: The government’s revenue will decline.
options.D: There will be more of the good imported.

Country X places a tariff of 20% on steel products imported from country Y. Country Y retaliates with a 20% tariff on computers imported from country X. What is a certain economic consequence of these actions?

options.A: The balance of payments of country X and country Y will remain unchanged.
options.B: The exchange rate value on which trade between the two countries is based will be maintained.
options.C: The profits and employment of domestic firms in both countries will be preserved.
options.D: The volume of bilateral trade between country X and country Y will be reduced.

questions.questionText: A country has a floating exchange rate. An increase in which variable within that country can cause its exchange rate to appreciate?

options.A: employment levels
options.B: income levels
options.C: interest rates
options.D: price levels

The graph shows the change in the current account of Belgium’s balance of payments from 2016 to 2017. 3.6 US$ billion –2.8 2016 2017 What will be the most likely impact of the change shown by the graph on Belgium’s domestic economy?

options.A: a fall in the rate of economic growth
options.B: a fall in the foreign currency reserves
options.C: a fall in the number of unemployed
options.D: a fall in the rate of inflation

questions.questionText: What is an example of the use of monetary policy?

options.A: a cut in the rate of corporation tax
options.B: a reduction in interest rates
options.C: a switch from direct to indirect taxation
options.D: the introduction of maximum price controls to reduce inflation

questions.questionText: Which policy would be likely to increase inflation?

options.A: an increase in income tax
options.B: an increase in interest rates
options.C: limiting the amount banks can lend
options.D: raising the level of import tariffs

questions.questionText: What are the components of aggregate demand?

options.A: consumption + investment + government spending + (exports – imports)
options.B: consumption + investment + taxation – (exports – imports)
options.C: consumption + saving + taxation – (exports – imports)
